Technical & price structure: In plain terms: ADIB is the UAE’s most profitable bank — a 28.8% return on equity built on deposits that are 91% current-and-savings — and it is priced for it: 3.31× book against a sector at 1.55×. Five lenses put fair value at AED 17.9–23.5, with a weighted central of AED 21.23 — about 2.4% below the price. On the payout it has held for five straight years (48.5–49.9% of profit), the dividend model alone says AED 22.5; give it credit for the surplus capital a slowing growth rate frees up and the FCFE ceiling is AED 23.5. The crux is durability: at our cost of equity the price already implies a 26% return on equity forever, better than management’s own 25% 2030 target. The bull case (~AED 23) is that the moat is structural and holds; the conservative case (~AED 18) is what the sector actually pays for this return today. What moves it near-term is whether the Strait of Hormuz stays open and how the UAE’s new minimum tax lands.

How is the Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank valuation calculated? — The study triangulates five lenses — a dividend discount model (the primary lens, given ADIB’s payout has not left 48.5–49.9% in five years); a full multi-period residual-income build; an FCFE equity DCF; ROE-adjusted relative multiples (dual-framed against two sector marks); and a through-cycle normalized-earnings floor — then expresses the result as a 50,000-path Monte Carlo probability distribution built on the UAE market’s own fitted calibration. Every assumption is visible and editable in the free Excel model.
